chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Zurāra, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), who said:
From what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught ʿAlī (peace be upon him), he said: 'Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his guest.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hospitality based on the Prophet's teaching to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this narration highlights the transmission of prophetic wisdom to Imam ʿAlī, framing hospitality not merely as etiquette but as a definitive sign of sincere belief in Allah and the Hereafter. In Shia scholarly tradition, this link underscores that social conduct is an outward manifestation of inner theological conviction, elevating the guest's right to a spiritual obligation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Is’haq Bin Abdul Aziz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> taught Ali<sup>asws</sup> - he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who believed in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so let him be benevolent with his guest’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd al-’Aziz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Of the matters that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, taught to Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was his saying, “Whoever believes in Allah and in the Day of Judgment, he must honor his guest.’””
